subject: Prompt-set ablation & regression: playbook + exception path
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@brighthealth.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected quality drop after v2 promptset rollout

Hi Marissa / David —

We rolled v2 of the prompt set into our staging A/B yesterday (traffic split 50/50) and our clinical QA team reported a clear drop in correctness for the symptom-mapping task on the control cohort. The model is hallucinating contraindications in ~8% of the samples vs ~1.5% baseline.

Claire (copied) ran a quick ablation and believes the new few-shot examples in prompt-set-v2.csv are the likely cause. We need a short playbook and an exception path — we cannot push to prod with this regression. Can Redwood help coordinate a rollback + targeted re-eval plan?

What we need from you today:
- A short remediation checklist we can follow to rollback safely to v1 if needed
- Acceptance criteria for re-run of prompt-set variants (what metrics/thresholds do you need?)
- A proposal for an A/B re-test (sample size, timeline)

Thanks — this is time-sensitive for our April go-live.

—Anita
Senior Product, BrightHealth

Attachments: prompt-set-v2.csv (30KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Anita Rao <anita@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:05:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected quality drop after v2 promptset rollout

Anita —

Thanks for the heads up and for the ablation notes, Claire. Sorry you hit this in staging. We should treat this as a gated regression and run a short playbook before any prod decision. Proposal below (high level) — I can own the coordination and stand up a quick channel with your QA folks.

1) Immediate mitigation (today):
- Pause the v2 cohort (we can flip traffic back to v1 within 15m). David, please confirm routing and whether a live rollback will require cache flushes.
- Snapshot logs and example trace IDs from the failing cases (Anita, can you share 20 representative traces?).

2) Short-term re-eval (48–72h):
- Run a focused A/B with the most-impacted prompt variants (we'll treat the problematic few-shot examples as variables). Suggested sample: 1,000 scored instances per arm to detect a ~5% absolute drop with power ~0.8.
- Acceptance criteria: hallucination rate <= 2.5% AND semantic-match F1 within 95% of v1 baseline. Lauren, confirm if those thresholds map to your SLA gating.

3) Exception path (if v2 fails):
- Roll back to v1 in prod (if staged) and open a regression ticket RD-5421 with prioritization for prompt engineering.
- Schedule joint triage with product + ML + CS to iterate on prompt content and re-test.

I attached a short playbook draft (regression_playbook_v1.md) and the current prompt-set-v2.csv you sent.

I can be on a call at 11:00 PT to run through steps with your team.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: regression_playbook_v1.md (18KB), prompt-set-v2.csv (30KB)

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Anita Rao <anita@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 14:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected quality drop after v2 promptset rollout

Marissa/Anita —

I paused the v2 experiment at 14:05 PT and routed traffic back to v1. Quick notes on the technical side:
- Rolling back is a config flip; no model redeploy required. We will, however, need to invalidate the KV prefix cache for the prompt namespace to ensure no stale cached tokens remain. That should be a 2–5 minute ops window.
- I pulled 25 failing trace IDs from staged logs and saved them in the shared Drive link below. Helpful for prompt debugging.

Dev, can you validate the targeted A/B harness? Ideally we run the A/B with identical hardware and same seed ranges to reduce noise. Also, if we add a quantization tweak later, we should run it in separate experiments.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-promptsets

—David
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@brighthealth.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 08:17:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected quality drop after v2 promptset rollout

Folks —

I sketched an A/B harness for the focused re-eval and a short exception runbook. TL;DR: we can do a 1k-per-arm split in 24h if BrightHealth can provide the sample bucket and expected labeling cadence. Key technical points:

- Harness: isolate the prompt variable by running the same model binary and runtime config. Configure per-request tags so we can slice traces by prompt-variant-id.
- Cache: ensure prefix cache invalidation only for the experiment namespace to avoid disturbing other customers. David handled the traffic flip; I'll do a dry-run of the cache invalidation in staging today.
- Instrumentation: add a custom metric for "contra_hallucination_rate" (binary label from your QA) and surface it on the Redwood Console dashboard for the experiment.
- Rollback policy: automatic fallback to v1 if hallucination_rate crosses 4% at any time during the test window. Manual gating at end of run uses the acceptance criteria Marissa suggested.

I attached the A/B plan notes (ab-plan-notes.pdf) and an example Prometheus query we'll use.

—Dev Patel
SRE / Inference Ops

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@brighthealth.ai>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected quality drop after v2 promptset rollout

Thanks team — good progress. Quick summary + next actions (finalizing playbook):

- Today: David confirmed v2 paused and traffic back to v1; Dev will validate cache invalidation dry-run in staging.
- By EOD Thu: BrightHealth to upload 20 representative failing traces and the 1k test sample bucket (Anita).
- A/B run (target): Fri 9:00 PT start, 24h run, 1,000 instances per arm. Observability: contra_hallucination_rate + semantic-match F1.
- Acceptance criteria (for green): hallucination_rate <= 2.5% AND semantic-match F1 >= 95% of v1 baseline across the test bucket. Fail -> rollback + prompt-engineering sprint.

If the run passes, we'll move with a staged prod rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with a 6-hour watch per step and automatic fallback policies enabled. If it fails, RD-5421 becomes P0 for prompt engineers and we'll schedule a joint war room.

I'll update the regression_playbook_v1.md with these tasks and turn this into a short runbook we can attach to the ticket. Thanks everyone for the quick turn.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: regression_playbook_v1.md (updated)
